questions.text: A building spirals upward asymmetrically, tilted at an angle as if frozen mid-motion, constructed from iron and technological apparatus. It was designed as a revolutionary monument but never built. Which movement and architect does this describe?

options.text: De Stijl, Gerrit Rietveld
Expressionism, Erich Mendelsohn
Constructivism, Vladimir Tatlin
Constructivism, Konstantin Melnikov

rationale.a: De Stijl architecture uses orthogonal geometry and primary colors, not spiraling asymmetrical forms.
rationale.b: Mendelsohn's Expressionism pursued curved, wave-like forms evocative of emotional response, not technological apparatus or revolutionary intent.
rationale.d: Melnikov was a Constructivist architect, but his work (like Melnikov House) differed from Tatlin's; the spiral tower specifically belongs to Tatlin.
rationale.correct: This describes the Tatlin Tower (1920), an unbuilt Constructivist design exemplifying asymmetry, dynamism, technological apparatus, and revolutionary symbolism.
rationale.takeaway: This describes the Tatlin Tower (1920), an unbuilt Constructivist design exemplifying asymmetry, dynamism, technological apparatus, and revolutionary symbolism.

questions.text: De Stijl and Constructivism both rejected ornament and pursued abstraction, but they differed fundamentally in their formal language. Which statement accurately distinguishes them?

options.text: De Stijl emphasized asymmetry and technological apparatus; Constructivism pursued orthogonal order and universal harmony, which is not accurate
De Stijl pursued systematic orthogonal geometry and primary colors; Constructivism embraced asymmetry, dynamism, and revolutionary gesture.
De Stijl was a movement of structural expressionism; Constructivism pursued rational, grid-based aesthetics, which is a common misconception
De Stijl emerged from Soviet revolutionary ideology; Constructivism originated in the Netherlands, which is historically incorrect

rationale.a: This reverses the two movements' formal characteristics.
rationale.c: Constructivism, not De Stijl, pursued structural expressionism; De Stijl pursued rational, planar abstraction.
rationale.d: De Stijl originated in the Netherlands, but Constructivism emerged from Soviet Russia, not the reverse.
rationale.correct: De Stijl's signature is orthogonal planes, primary colors (red, yellow, blue), and white space expressing universal harmony. Constructivism's signature is asymmetrical, bold, and dynamically tilted forms expressing technological power and communist ideology.
rationale.takeaway: Constructivism's signature is asymmetrical, bold, and dynamically tilted forms expressing technological power and communist ideology.
